arxiv-1809-01878.title: Mitochondrial heterogeneity
arxiv-1809-01878.creator: Juvid Aryaman 1,2,3 , Iain G. Johnston 4,5 and Nick S. Jones 1,5,∗
arxiv-1809-01878.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Juvid Aryaman 1,2,3 , Iain G. Johnston 4,5 and Nick S. Jones 1,5,∗. Cell-to-cell heterogeneity drives a range of (patho)physiologically important phenomena, such as cell fate and chemotherapeutic resistance. The role of metabolism, and particularly mitochondria, is increasingly being recognised as an important explanatory factor in cell-to-cell heterogeneity. Most eukaryotic cells possess a population of mitochondria, in the sense that mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is held in multiple copies per cell, where the sequence of each molecule can vary.

arxiv-2103-11316.title: Automated Software Vulnerability Assessment with Concept Drift
arxiv-2103-11316.creator: Triet H. M. Le, Bushra Sabir, and M. Ali Babar
arxiv-2103-11316.description: Abstract Software Engineering researchers are increasingly using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to automate Software Vulnerabilities (SVs) assessment using the descriptions in public repositories. However, the existing NLP-based approaches suffer from concept drift . This problem is caused by a lack of proper treatment of new (out-of-vocabulary) terms for the evaluation of unseen SVs over time.

arxiv-2110-01461.title: Neutron star crustal properties from relativistic mean-field models and bulk parameters effects
arxiv-2110-01461.creator: M. Dutra, C. H. Lenzi, W. de Paula, and O. Lourenço
arxiv-2110-01461.description: Abstract We calculate crustal properties of neutron stars, namely, mass ( M crust M_{\rm crust} ), radius ( R crust R_{\rm crust} ) and fraction of moment of inertia ( Δ ​ I / I \Delta I/I ) from parametrizations of hadronic relativistic mean-field (RMF) model consistent with symmetric and asymmetric nuclear matter constraints, as well as some stellar boundaries.

arxiv-2303-02611.title: A Solution to the 1-2-3 Conjecture
arxiv-2303-02611.creator: Ralph Keusch
arxiv-2303-02611.description: Abstract We show that for every graph without isolated edge, the edges can be assigned weights from { 1 , 2 , 3 } \{1,2,3\} so that no two neighbors receive the same sum of incident edge weights. This solves a conjecture of Karoński, Łuczak, and Thomason from 2004. 1 Introduction Let G=(V,E) be a simple graph.

arxiv-2402-10966.title: Non-contact photoacoustic imaging with a silicon photonics-based Laser Doppler Vibrometer
arxiv-2402-10966.creator: Emiel Dieussaert, Roel Baets, Hilde Jans, Xavier Rottenberg, Yanlu Li
arxiv-2402-10966.description: Abstract Photoacoustic imaging has emerged as a powerful, non-invasive modality for various biomedical applications. Conventional photoacoustic systems require contact-based ultrasound detection and expensive and bulky high-power lasers for the excitation. The use of contact-based detectors involves the risk of contamination, which is undesirable for most biomedical applications.

arxiv-2405-14095.title: Abrupt X-to-O-wave structural field transition in presence of anomalous dispersion
arxiv-2405-14095.creator: Layton A. Hall 1, Ayman F. Abouraddy 1,∗
arxiv-2405-14095.description: Abstract All linear, propagation-invariant, paraxial pulsed beams are spatiotemporally X-shaped (conical waves) in absence of group-velocity dispersion (GVD), or in presence of normal GVD. It is known, however, that such conical waves become O-shaped in presence of anomalous GVD, resulting in a field profile that is circularly symmetric in space and time.

arxiv-2409-00245.title: Preprocessing to Reduce the Search Space for Odd Cycle Transversal
arxiv-2409-00245.creator: Bart M. P. Jansen, Yosuke Mizutani, Blair D. Sullivan, Ruben F. A. Verhaegh
arxiv-2409-00245.description: Abstract The NP-hard Odd Cycle Transversal problem asks for a minimum vertex set whose removal from an undirected input graph G G breaks all odd cycles, and thereby yields a bipartite graph. The problem is well-known to be fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the size k k of the desired solution.

arxiv-2409-08674.title: The Method of Searching for Rotations of the Polarization Position Angle of Quasars
arxiv-2409-08674.creator: S. S. Savchenko, D. A. Morozova, S. G. Jorstad, D. A. Blinov, G. A. Borman, A. A. Vasilyev, T. S. Grishina, A. V. Zhovtan, E. N. Kopatskaya, E. G. Larionova, I. S. Troitskiy, Yu. V. Troitskaya, E. V. Shishkina, E. A. Shkodkina
arxiv-2409-08674.description: Abstract Observations of quasars show that the polarization position angle of the emission coming from them varies greatly over time, including periods called rotations during which the angle changes in an orderly manner. The study proposes a method for identifying such events and assessing their statistical significance.

arxiv-2505-23445.title: The Strong, Weak and Benign Goodhart’s law. An independence-free and paradigm-agnostic formalisation
arxiv-2505-23445.creator: Adrien Majka, El-Mahdi El-Mhamdi
arxiv-2505-23445.description: Abstract Goodhart’s law is a famous adage in policy-making that states that “When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure”. As machine learning models and the optimisation capacity to train them grow, growing empirical evidence reinforced the belief in the validity of this law without however being formalised.

arxiv-2601-04966.creator: Zixuan Feng, Qiushi Chen, Paul Griffin, Le Bao
arxiv-2601-04966.description: Abstract Drug overdose deaths, including from opioids, remain a significant public health threat to the United States (US). To abate the harms of opioid misuse, understanding its prevalence at the local level is crucial for stakeholders in communities to develop response strategies that effectively use limited resources.

pmc-11548659.title: Evaluating Alternative Registration Planes in Imageless, Computer-Assisted Navigation Systems for Direct Anterior Total Hip Arthroplasty
pmc-11548659.creator: John E Farey, Yuan Chai, Joshua Xu, Vincent Maes, Ameneh Sadeghpour, Neri A Baker, Jonathan M Vigdorchik, William L Walter, Iulian I Iordachita
pmc-11548659.description: (1) Background: Imageless computer navigation systems have the potential to improve the accuracy of acetabular cup position in total hip arthroplasty (THA). Popular imageless navigation methods include locating the patient in a three-dimensional space (registration method) while using a baseline to angle the acetabular cup (reference plane).

pmc-12452344.title: Implementing a Functional Group Analysis Activity to Support Student Learning in Medicinal Chemistry: A Three-Year Experience
pmc-12452344.creator: Ansel Belani, Jitendra D Belani, Conxita Mestres
pmc-12452344.description: Many pharmacy students begin medicinal chemistry with limited experience in chemical structure interpretation and reactivity patterns, making it difficult to connect foundational concepts to real-world drug behavior. We introduced a low-stakes functional group analysis activity that included peer discussion and a follow-up quiz to improve learning and reduce student anxiety.

pmc-12586957.title: Contentopic mapping in ventral and dorsal association cortex: The topographical organization of manipulable object information
pmc-12586957.creator: J Almeida, S Kristensen, Z Tal, A Fracasso
pmc-12586957.description: Highlights•We used population receptive field analysis to identify the topography of object information.•Contentopic maps representing mid-level object-related dimensions (e.g., object grasp) were observed in dorsal and ventral occipital cortex.•Contentopic maps are continuous, consistent across individuals, and specific to each dimension tested.•Contentopic maps are not fully derived from the eccentricity signatures of the visual stimuli used.

pmc-12595687.title: Perceived rehabilitation needs of older people with dementia
pmc-12595687.creator: Outi Mäenpää, Johanna Edgren, Mari Aaltonen, Lina van Aerschot, Jari Pirhonen, Jenni Kulmala
pmc-12595687.description: BackgroundRehabilitation is an umbrella term for actions that aim to optimise autonomy, life management, functioning, and well-being of older people. Physical rehabilitation supports physical functioning and daily activities. However, in dementia care, rehabilitation is an underutilised resource, and healthcare professionals describe challenges in implementing rehabilitation. Also, scientific knowledge of individual rehabilitation needs is relatively scarce.

pmc-12608998.title: Validation of a Dermatology-Focused Multimodal Large Language Model in Classification of Pigmented Skin Lesions
pmc-12608998.creator: Joshua Mijares, Neil Jairath, Andrew Zhang, Syril Keena T Que, Fabiano Bini
pmc-12608998.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown significant promise in augmenting diagnostic capabilities across medical specialties. Recent advancements in generative AI allow for synthesis and interpretation of complex clinical data including imaging and patient history to assess disease risk. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of a dermatology-trained multimodal large language model (DermFlow, Delaware, USA) in assessing malignancy risk of pigmented skin lesions.

pmc-12731135.title: Atrazine Induces Reproductive Toxicity in an In Vitro Spermatogenesis (IVS) Model
pmc-12731135.creator: Monsikan Chaiyakit, Rangsun Parnpai, In K. Cho
pmc-12731135.description: Background/Objectives: Atrazine (ATZ) is a widely used herbicide, and most studies of its reproductive toxicity have been conducted in vivo using animal models, where ATZ disrupts redox homeostasis, leading to male reproductive dysfunction. However, its molecular mechanisms of action in human spermatogenic cells remain poorly understood.

pmc-12979869.title: Six-Month SIRSI Scores and Return to Sport After Shoulder Stabilization in Adolescent Athletes
pmc-12979869.creator: Carolina Pavlenco, Bilal Khilfeh, Xing Wang, Michael Saper
pmc-12979869.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Psychological readiness is increasingly recognized as a return-to-sport (RTS) determinant after shoulder stabilization surgery. The Shoulder Instability–Return to Sport After Injury (SIRSI) score is a tool to assess psychological recovery, yet prognostic value at intermediate postoperative milestones remains unclear.Purpose/Hypothesis:The purpose was to evaluate whether 6-month SIRSI scores relate to 1-year patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and RTS in adolescents after shoulder stabilization surgery.

pmc-13066834.title: Phenotyping preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) using quantitative high-resolution computed tomography imaging features
pmc-13066834.creator: Jun Hu, Zhujin Shen, Tong Su, Yu Fang, Wen Yang, Chen Chu, Xin Peng, Chao Zou, Jian He, Xiaoyan Xin
pmc-13066834.description: BackgroundPreserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) is characterized by decreased forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) with a preserved FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio. It is a highly prevalent and heterogeneous condition which is associated with increased risk of respiratory symptoms, developing airway limitation, and mortality. However, there are few radiological studies related to phenotyping of PRISm.

pmc-13141089.title: Future perspectives on the use of molecular assays for pathogen identification in neonatal sepsis: a survey study among members of the European Society for Paediatric Infectious Diseases
pmc-13141089.creator: Jip Groen, Martijn van der Kuip, Marc A Benninga, Tim de Meij, Hendrik J Niemarkt
pmc-13141089.description: of empiric antibiotic treatment, with many neonates exposed to prolonged therapy despite sterile BCs, specifically for early-onset NS.4 5 Molecular assays have been proposed to accelerate pathogen identification and support antibiotic stewardship.6 However, large-scale implementation has yet to follow. Understanding clinician perspectives is essential to guide future diagnostic implementation.

pmc-13265392.title: Awareness and Utilization of the Revised Second International Staging System (R2‐ISS) and 1q21 Gain/Amplification Testing: A Nationwide Web‐Based Survey of Hematologists in Japan
pmc-13265392.creator: Nami Tagami, Heigoroh Shirai, Ichiro Hanamura
pmc-13265392.description: BackgroundAlthough the multiple myeloma (MM) treatment landscape has significantly advanced, MM remains an incurable disease. Accurate risk stratification and its broad clinical implementation are essential for optimizing treatment strategies. International Staging System (ISS), its revised versions (R‐ISS and R2‐ISS), and cytogenetic testing for abnormalities such as chromosome 1q21 gain/amplification are recognized tools for risk assessment.

pmc-13345263.creator: Niklas Kiermeyer, Tim Lenfers, Amin Dada, Julian Friedrich, Sameh Khattab, Eric Knop, Jan Egger, Markus Pauly, Andreas Jung, Grégoire Montavon, Jens T. Siveke, Marcel Wiesweg, Stefan Kasper, Ulf P. Neumann, Frederick Klauschen, Sylvia Hartmann, Martin Schuler, Philipp Keyl, Jens Kleesiek, Julius Key
pmc-13345263.description: In medical documentation, vast amounts of unstructured text are generated that are still underutilized in current prognostic models. We investigate the potential of self-hosted large language models (LLM) to extract clinically meaningful, patient-specific information from routine clinical notes for personalized risk stratification in cancer care.

pmc-13396667.title: Targeting the intrinsically disordered AR-NTD through a machine learning-based enhanced sampling workflow
pmc-13396667.creator: Kai Zhu, Huating Wang, Jintu Zhang, Renling Hu, Linlong Jiang, Hui Zhang, Yu Kang, Tingjun Hou, Dan Li
pmc-13396667.description: Targeting the intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain of the androgen receptor (AR-NTD) represents a promising strategy to overcome resistance in prostate cancer. However, its inherent lack of a stable tertiary structure and highly dynamic conformational ensemble pose formidable challenges for rational drug design.

pmc-13513842.title: Impact of IL6 and IL18 Promoter Polymorphisms on Circulating Cytokine Levels, Gene Expression, and Susceptibility to Rheumatoid Arthritis
pmc-13513842.creator: Viktoria Vasileva, Georgi Vasilev, Mariana Ivanova, Lyuba Miteva, Irena Manolova
pmc-13513842.description: Our study examined the impact of IL6 −174 G/C (rs1800795) and IL18 −607 C/A (rs1946518) promoter polymorphisms on susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and protein/mRNA levels. RA patients had significantly higher serum IL-6 and IL-18 levels than controls; healthy men had higher IL-18 than women (p < 0.001).

pmc-13679366.title: Prevalence and spectrum of variants in homologous recombination repair genes in ovarian cancer in Latin America: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13679366.creator: Elizabeth Vargas-Castellanos, Natalia Santiago-Tovar, Luisa Murcia-Soriano, Ariana Patino-Herrera, Rafael Parra-Medina, Julian C Riano-Moreno
pmc-13679366.description: BACKGROUNDOvarian cancer is a major cause of gynecologic cancer mortality worldwide, with disproportionately poor outcomes in Latin America (LATAM). Variants in homologous recombination repair genes, especially BRCA1/2, are predictive biomarkers for platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors. However, data on the prevalence and spectrum of homologous recombination repair variants in LATAM populations remain limited.

pmc-13685264.title: A latent genetic factor underlies multiple component phenotypes of cerebral small vessel disease
pmc-13685264.creator: Yan Zeng, Xiaoqian Huang, Yubiao Yang, Chun Guo
pmc-13685264.description: BackgroundCerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) encompasses white matter hyperintensities (WMH), enlarged perivascular spaces (PVS), intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), small vessel stroke (SVS), and cognitive impairment—phenotypes that frequently co-occur yet have been studied as independent genetic endpoints. Whether a shared genetic architecture underlies these co-occurring cSVD-related phenotypes remains unclear.
